spec.title: Appliance health
spec.description: One row per appliance region. Each cell is a sparkline over the dashboard time range; the number beside it is the reduction: Status and Reconcile age = last value, CPU / Memory / Requests = mean, Disk and 5xx = max (worst filesystem, worst minute). Reconcile age turns red past 15 minutes, which is when the node has stopped reconciling. Status counts how many of the region's two scrapes answered, the host exporter and Caddy: the word is the state now (up = both, partial = one, down = neither) and the grey bars are the same count across the window, full height for both, half for one, a stub for neither. A notch in the bars is an incident, and its position is when. The bar colour is constant and means nothing. Requests and 5xx read no data rather than zero when the Caddy scrape is dark. Click a region to open its tab.

spec.expr:
sum by (region) (
  rate(caddy_http_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name=~"appliance-.*-caddy", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)", code=~"5.."}[5m])
) * 60
or
sum by (region) (
  rate(caddy_http_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name=~"appliance-.*-caddy", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}[5m])
) * 0

spec.title: Request rate
spec.description: Every public request the appliance served, split by site and HTTP method, stacked so the top of the stack is total traffic. Method is the only operation kind Caddy sees: an S3 PutObject is a PUT to a bucket path, so PUT against the s3. host is the upload path. Read from the duration histogram's count, because caddy_http_requests_total carries neither a code nor a method label.

spec.title: Server errors
spec.description: 5xx split by site, handler and code. A 502 is Caddy failing to reach the upstream; a 500 came from Piri or Ingot itself.

spec.title: Response time
spec.description: Round-trip time to last byte, per site: caddy_http_request_duration_seconds, the whole request. TTFB is the panel beside it. The average is sum/count; p95 reads the histogram buckets.

spec.expr:
sum by (host) (
  rate(caddy_http_request_duration_seconds_sum{service_name=~"appliance-.*-caddy", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}[5m])
)
/
sum by (host) (
  rate(caddy_http_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name=~"appliance-.*-caddy", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}[5m])
)

spec.title: Time since last deploy
spec.description: Age of each project's last successful pass, from the deploy stamp the reconcile timer writes through the textfile collector. The timer runs every five minutes, so a reconcile age past the 15-minute threshold line means the node has stopped reconciling. apps and platform move only when that project actually deployed, so they climb between releases and that is normal.

spec.title: Error rate
spec.description: 5xx responses as a share of everything the site served. The trailing `or ... * 0` holds the line at zero for a site with traffic and no errors; a site with no data at all drops out rather than reading zero. Threshold lines at 1% and 5%. The axis carries a soft max of 5%, so an idle panel sits at 0-5% with the threshold lines visible instead of Grafana inventing a 0-10000% range for an all-zero series; a real error rate above 5% expands it.

spec.expr:
sum by (host) (
  rate(caddy_http_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name=~"appliance-.*-caddy", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)", code=~"5.."}[5m])
)
/
sum by (host) (
  rate(caddy_http_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name=~"appliance-.*-caddy", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}[5m])
)
or
sum by (host) (
  rate(caddy_http_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name=~"appliance-.*-caddy", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}[5m])
) * 0

spec.title: Ingress / egress
spec.description: Bytes in and out through Caddy, which is every public request the region serves. Taken from the histograms' _sum, so the figure is exact and does not depend on the size buckets. The node exporter's network collector is not shipped, so this is the appliance's traffic rather than the host interface's.

spec.title: TTFB
spec.description: Time to first byte, p95, per site and method. caddy_http_response_duration_seconds is Caddy's own "times to first byte in response bodies" histogram, distinct from request_duration_seconds, which is the whole round trip. Split by method so uploads can be read apart from reads.

spec.title: Containers
spec.description: Each appliance container Alloy has labelled, read from cAdvisor's series rather than from a scrape target of its own -- containers have none, which is why the Scrapes panel above cannot show them. Not quite every container on the box: the deny-list drops the one that exits by design, and the host's own containers carry no appliance service_name, so they never appear. Empty on a stage that runs no cAdvisor, which today is dev, and indistinguishable there from a stage whose containers have all been removed. These are the windows `Appliance container is not running` alerts on, but without that rule's cAdvisor-liveness gate, so the two agree except in one case: if cAdvisor itself dies, every row here goes down within five minutes while the alert stays deliberately quiet, because the alternative is every container paging at once. A separate rule on the scrape's own health is what covers that. A row reads up if any sample landed in the last five minutes, so a container that stops reads up for up to five minutes more, and one that restarts faster than that never reads down at all.

spec.title: Scrapes
spec.description: Whether Alloy's scrapes for this region answered: the host exporter, and Caddy. It says whether to believe the panels built on those two -- the host metrics and the reconcile age come from the first, the request and error panels from the second -- and when one goes dark its panels read no data rather than zero, which looks much like zero at a glance. It does not cover the whole tab: Ingot's own metrics arrive by a route with no up of its own, so those panels can go blank with both rows here still green. Containers have no scrape either and are in the panel below. A scrape that is attempted and fails reads down; if Alloy itself stops, no up series is produced at all and the row goes blank rather than red, which is why the rule for a node that has gone away tests for absence instead. Two boxes in one stage and region share service_name, and no label here would separate them: the only label telling those two rows apart is node, and every node value today names a stage and at most a region.

spec.title: CPU
spec.description: Share of a core spent in each non-idle mode, averaged across cores. Stacked, so the top of the stack is total CPU busy.

spec.title: Memory used
spec.description: Fraction of RAM not available to a new allocation. MemAvailable already discounts reclaimable cache, so this is closer to real pressure than used/total.

spec.title: Load average
spec.description: Run-queue length. Compare against the box's core count: sustained load5 above that is saturation.

spec.title: Disk I/O
spec.description: Throughput per block device from the diskstats collector.

spec.title: Disk Space Usage
spec.description: Used fraction per real filesystem. Not stacked: these are independent ratios and a stacked total of them means nothing.

spec.expr:
1 - node_filesystem_avail_bytes{service_name=~"appliance-.*-host", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)", fstype!~"tmpfs|vfat|squashfs|overlay", mountpoint!~"/boot.*"}
  / node_filesystem_size_bytes{service_name=~"appliance-.*-host", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)", fstype!~"tmpfs|vfat|squashfs|overlay", mountpoint!~"/boot.*"}

spec.title: Inode Usage
spec.description: Used inodes per filesystem. A volume with free bytes and no free inodes fails writes the same way a full one does.

spec.expr:
1 - node_filesystem_files_free{service_name=~"appliance-.*-host", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)", fstype!~"tmpfs|vfat|squashfs|overlay", mountpoint!~"/boot.*"}
  / node_filesystem_files{service_name=~"appliance-.*-host", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)", fstype!~"tmpfs|vfat|squashfs|overlay", mountpoint!~"/boot.*"}

spec.title: Ingot local disk
spec.description: Bytes Ingot holds under its data_dir, stacked by directory, against local_blob_max_bytes (dashed; absent when no budget is set). spool is bodies being written or awaiting upload, which eviction cannot touch; cache is bodies the provider already holds, which the sweeper evicts oldest first to stay under the budget. Ingot's README, "Local disk", says what each holds.

spec.title: Ingot stalled uploads
spec.description: Bytes of bodies whose upload has stalled, one line per state: intents still spooled (the body never left the node) or uploading (it may have reached its provider) an hour after their last state change. Nothing reclaims a failed PUT's yet (a multipart part's goes with its session), and they count against the budget. Anything above zero is an upload that did not finish; a rising line means it keeps happening.

spec.title: Ingot local removals
spec.description: Files removed from local disk per second, by reason: released (object deleted or overwritten), parked (multipart part handed to its provider), budget (evicted to stay under the budget), budget_forced (evicted inside the retention windows because the budget needed it), orphan (a leftover no upload names), accepted (dropped on accept, with cache_writes: false). Steady budget_forced means the budget is too small for the ingest rate and read working set.

spec.title: Ingot local read share
spec.description: The share of object-body reads Ingot served from local disk rather than from the provider over the network, which is what the cache is for. Low when the budget is small against the read working set, or with cache_writes: false.

spec.expr:
sum by (node) (rate(ingot_local_blobs_reads_total{service_name=~"appliance-.*-ingot", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)", tier="local"}[15m]))
/
sum by (node) (rate(ingot_local_blobs_reads_total{service_name=~"appliance-.*-ingot", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}[15m]))

spec.title: Ingot catalog on Forge
spec.description: Catalog bytes Ingot has shipped to Forge and not released, summed over the node's buckets: the segments' CARs, not their index blobs. Nothing collects dead catalog blocks yet, so the shipped line only grows until a bucket is deleted. Dead on arrival is the part already superseded when its segment shipped, over the segments Ingot measured; unmeasured is the shipped bytes it didn't measure, such as every segment shipped before it began measuring. Dead counts only buckets with a completed catalog walk, as of that walk for a bucket whose root has moved since; "Ingot catalog walk coverage" says how much that leaves out. Ingot's README, "Catalog storage", says what each gauge measures.

spec.title: Ingot dead catalog share
spec.description: How much of the node's catalog on Forge is dead. The two walked lines cover the buckets with a completed catalog walk, each bucket's live and dead bytes from the same moment: all dead bytes, and the part that died after its segment shipped. The gap between them is, roughly, what those buckets' measured segments held dead on arrival. Died after shipping also includes every dead block of segments Ingot didn't measure, so it reads high while unmeasured bytes are large ("Ingot catalog on Forge"). Dead on arrival, measured segments, covers every bucket. The dead line is a floor: a walk counts a block once per link to it, so a block several others link to counts as live more than once, and a bucket whose walk reached more than it has shipped counts as none dead. Died after shipping is one too, once unmeasured bytes are small.

spec.expr:
sum by (node) (ingot_catalog_dead_bytes{service_name=~"appliance-.*-ingot", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"})
/
(sum by (node) (ingot_catalog_live_bytes{service_name=~"appliance-.*-ingot", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"} + ingot_catalog_dead_bytes{service_name=~"appliance-.*-ingot", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}) > 0)

sum by (node) (ingot_catalog_dead_after_ship_bytes{service_name=~"appliance-.*-ingot", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"})
/
(sum by (node) (ingot_catalog_live_bytes{service_name=~"appliance-.*-ingot", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"} + ingot_catalog_dead_bytes{service_name=~"appliance-.*-ingot", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}) > 0)

sum by (node) (ingot_catalog_dead_on_arrival_bytes{service_name=~"appliance-.*-ingot", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"})
/
(sum by (node) (ingot_catalog_forge_bytes{service_name=~"appliance-.*-ingot", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"} - ingot_catalog_unmeasured_bytes{service_name=~"appliance-.*-ingot", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}) > 0)

spec.title: Ingot catalog walk coverage
spec.description: Catalog bytes on Forge, stacked by the state of each bucket's last catalog walk: current (the bucket's root hasn't moved since), stale (it has) or never walked. The dead figures speak only for current and stale buckets. Ingot walks a bucket only while it holds read authority borrowed from a recent request in the bucket's space, so a bucket with no request since Ingot started isn't walked: one walked before then stays current or stale, and one never walked stays in never. A bucket goes stale with its next write and isn't walked again until catalog_walk_interval (6h by default) after its last walk, so stale bytes are normal. A stopped walker shows as stale bytes that don't return to current within that interval, while new buckets stay in never.

spec.title: Ingot largest bucket catalogs
spec.description: The ten buckets with the most catalog bytes on Forge. Ingot labels each bucket by its space DID, never by its name. The top ten is taken at each point, so over a long range the legend can list more than ten buckets, each with gaps where it fell out.

spec.expr: topk(10, max by (node, space) (ingot_catalog_forge_bytes{service_name=~"appliance-.*-ingot", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}))

spec.title: Ingot multipart acceptance wait
spec.description: How long the oldest multipart part still waiting for acceptance has waited, per node. Ingot accepts a part's blobs in the background while the client is still uploading, normally within seconds; a value that keeps climbing means the acceptor is failing or not running, and CompleteMultipartUpload answers OperationAborted for an upload with a part that has not been accepted. The 'Ingot multipart acceptance is stuck' alert fires above 10 minutes.

spec.title: Ingot multipart acceptance failures
spec.description: Per node, per minute: acceptor passes that failed (they are retried after a backoff), and CompleteMultipartUpload requests answered OperationAborted because a part they name was still waiting for acceptance. The AWS CLI treats that answer as a failed upload. Failed passes with no deferred Completes are retries that caught up.

spec.title: Piri CommP queue
spec.description: Accepted blobs at the entry of Piri's aggregation pipeline, per node. Held blobs are waiting out pdp.aggregation.commp.delay (one hour by default) before their CommP is computed, so the line tracks the ingest rate times the delay. Due blobs are past the delay with no CommP task yet; the task engine claims them within a poll, so this line sits at zero, and one that keeps rising means claims have stopped.

spec.title: Piri blobs released before aggregation
spec.description: Blobs whose removal cancelled their pipeline row before they were folded into an aggregate, per hour and per node. before_commp ones were released inside the CommP delay and cost nothing; after_commp ones had their CommP computed and piece parked, which finalization cleans up. The before_commp share is what the delay is saving.

spec.title: Piri releases caught by a CommP delay of N
spec.description: Of the blobs released before aggregation over the last day, the share that was released within 1, 5, 15, 30 and 60 minutes of acceptance, per node. Each line is the fraction of those releases a CommP delay of that length catches, so the 60m line is what the default saves today and the gap between lines is what a shorter or longer delay would change. Blobs that are never released do not appear here; the lines only compare delays against each other.

spec.expr:
sum by (node) (increase(piri_pdp_pipeline_cancelled_age_seconds_bucket{job="forge/piri", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)", le="60"}[1d]))
/
sum by (node) (increase(piri_pdp_pipeline_cancelled_age_seconds_count{job="forge/piri", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}[1d]))

sum by (node) (increase(piri_pdp_pipeline_cancelled_age_seconds_bucket{job="forge/piri", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)", le="300"}[1d]))
/
sum by (node) (increase(piri_pdp_pipeline_cancelled_age_seconds_count{job="forge/piri", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}[1d]))

sum by (node) (increase(piri_pdp_pipeline_cancelled_age_seconds_bucket{job="forge/piri", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)", le="900"}[1d]))
/
sum by (node) (increase(piri_pdp_pipeline_cancelled_age_seconds_count{job="forge/piri", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}[1d]))

sum by (node) (increase(piri_pdp_pipeline_cancelled_age_seconds_bucket{job="forge/piri", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)", le="1800"}[1d]))
/
sum by (node) (increase(piri_pdp_pipeline_cancelled_age_seconds_count{job="forge/piri", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}[1d]))

sum by (node) (increase(piri_pdp_pipeline_cancelled_age_seconds_bucket{job="forge/piri", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)", le="3600"}[1d]))
/
sum by (node) (increase(piri_pdp_pipeline_cancelled_age_seconds_count{job="forge/piri", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}[1d]))

spec.title: Piri Postgres pool: acquires that waited
spec.description: Share of connection acquires from each Piri's PDP pool that waited because no connection was free, over 5 minutes. Every PDP task and every blob/accept shares this pool, sized by pool_max_conns on the Postgres URL. Occasional waits during a burst are fine; a sustained share above the line (a tenth) means accepts and tasks are queueing for the pool, and the fix is a bigger pool_max_conns.

spec.expr:
sum by (node, instance) (rate(piri_pdp_db_pool_acquires_waited_total{job="forge/piri", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}[5m]))
/ sum by (node, instance) (rate(piri_pdp_db_pool_acquires_total{job="forge/piri", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}[5m]))

spec.title: Piri Postgres pool: mean wait
spec.description: How long the acquires that waited spent waiting, on average over 5 minutes, per Piri. Read with the share that waited: a small share with a long wait is a few requests stuck behind a long task, a large share with a short wait is steady contention. No series while nothing has waited.

spec.expr:
sum by (node, instance) (rate(piri_pdp_db_pool_acquire_wait_seconds_total{job="forge/piri", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}[5m]))
/ sum by (node, instance) (rate(piri_pdp_db_pool_acquires_waited_total{job="forge/piri", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)"}[5m]))

spec.title: Piri Postgres pool: connections in use
spec.description: Connections callers hold in each Piri's PDP pool against its configured maximum. In use sitting at the maximum for sustained periods is the pool saturated, and the waits above follow.

spec.expr: max by (node, instance) (piri_pdp_db_pool_connections{job="forge/piri", appliance=~"$stage-.*", region=~"($region)", state="acquired"})

spec.title: Ingot unshipped catalog age
spec.description: How long the oldest catalog block journaled in Postgres has waited for its segment to ship to Forge, per node. Ingot journals each commit's new catalog blocks until their segment ships, and segments seal within seconds and ship right after, so this stays near zero. A value that keeps climbing means a segment has not shipped: the blocks are safe in Postgres, but that part of the catalog is not reaching Forge. The 'Ingot catalog shipping has stalled' alert fires above 30 minutes.

spec.title: Ingot unshipped catalog size
spec.description: Bytes of catalog blocks journaled in Postgres whose segment has not shipped to Forge yet, per node. Normally a few seconds of commits; growth goes with a climbing age on the panel beside this one.
